newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on crush data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on crush data.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended firm on Friday amid bullish news from USDA's weekly export sales and the U.S. Census figures, traders said.
USDA on Friday reported net sales of 100,000 tonnes of soymeal and 4,300 tonnes of soyoil.

U.S. Census Bureau monthly data, also issued Friday, showed there were 138 million bushels of soybeans crushed in December. But soymeal stocks fell from November's levels, suggesting demand was outpacing supply.
Soymeal stocks were reported at 239,686 tons, down from 259,217 tons in November and well below last year's 347,162 tons.
Stocks data indicated soyoil demand was not keeping pace with soymeal usage and stocks were building.
The Census report showed soyoil stocks at 915.1 million lbs, above November's 851.4 million lbs and last year's 585.4 million.
"The (cash) market is firm for meal but it's not nearly as firm for oil," one floor trader said. "Oil is up in sympathy as much as anything."
Soyoil closed 0.20 to 0.07 cent per lb higher with March up 0.11 at 24.21. Soymeal ended $2.60 to $0.20 higher with March up $2.20 at $238.10 a ton.
On the day, ADM sold 50 lots May soymeal, Cargill Inc sold 50 lots October and bought 50 lots July. E.D. and F. Man International bought 50 March and Cargill Investor Services bought 50 lots March.
In soyoil, Chicago Corp and Cargill Investor Services each sold 50 lots March. Iowa Grain sold 250 lots March. E.D. and F. Man International bought 50 lots March.

Soymeal volume was estimated at 13,000 lots, CBOT reported. That compared with Thursday's actual volume of 15,178 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated by CBOT at 8,000 lots, against Thursday's actual volume of 7,938.
